Note on N-S1 to N-S4 and N-E1, what a queue message is checked against.

Checked before a drain: the body parses as JSON into `EventBridgeEvent` (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:125`); if `detail-type` is empty the body must parse as an ASG lifecycle message and `LifecycleTransition` must equal one of two exact strings (`:168`, `:181-183`), after which the code stamps the lifecycle source itself (`:186`); `source` must be one of three exact service strings, and for two of them `detail-type` must be one of four exact strings (`:206-239`); for a state change, `strings.Contains` on the state (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/ec2-state-change-event.go:60`); for AWS Health, the service and event-category fields must each equal one fixed value (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/scheduled-change-event.go:78-86`); `detail.instance-id` must resolve through `DescribeInstances` under the handler's own credentials with a non-empty `PrivateDnsName` (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:365`, `:395-416`); and with `CHECK_TAG_BEFORE_DRAINING` at its default the instance must carry `ManagedTag` (`:438-442`, `:266-269`).

Not checked: `account`, `region` and `resources`, declared at `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/event-bridge.go:29`, `:31`, `:32` and read nowhere in the repository; no ARN is parsed; no signature, message attribute or sender identity is examined; nothing ties the message to this cluster beyond the instance tag; `instance-action` on the spot path is declared at `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/spot-itn-event.go:48` and never read; the rebalance detail carries only `instance-id` (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/rebalance-recommendation-event.go:45-47`); the lifecycle action token is never checked against anything in the tree. It reaches `CompleteLifecycleAction` at `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/asg-lifecycle-event.go:273`, after the drain, and `RecordLifecycleActionHeartbeat` at `:229`, which runs from a goroutine started by the pre-drain task at `:126`, first at that goroutine's first tick one interval later (`:188`, `:208-209`), and therefore during the drain whenever `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL` is set and the drain outlasts one interval; that value is -1 at both the code default (`NTH: pkg/config/config.go:254`) and the chart default (posture, `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/values.yaml:292`).

What the actor needs: the ability to place a message on that queue, a B2 position. The documented queue policy names only the service principals `events.amazonaws.com` and `sqs.amazonaws.com` (posture, `NTH: README.md:334-337`), so the position is not granted by that policy; which other principals hold send rights is set outside the tree (inferred, seam: SQS and IAM). Nothing in the message is verified against the cluster's own identity. The node resolution is `PrivateDnsName` from `DescribeInstances` (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:424`), then the `kubernetes.io/hostname` lookup at `NTH: pkg/node/node.go:655-672`, then `drain.RunNodeDrain` at `:171` under the service account in `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/templates/clusterrole.yaml:9-30` (posture).

Note on N-T4, N-I1 and N-E5, what `WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_FILE` reaches.

The read is `os.ReadFile(nthConfig.WebhookTemplateFile)`, at `NTH: pkg/webhook/webhook.go:45` on every post and at `:140` once at startup. It is a local filesystem read with no scheme and no path restriction, so it reaches any path the process can open in its own mount namespace: files baked into the image, files on mounted volumes, and anything else visible to uid 1000 in that container (posture, `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/values.yaml:38-43`). It does not reach a remote host and it does not reach another container (the mount-namespace boundary is inferred, seam: the kernel and the container runtime). `WEBHOOK_PROXY` and `WEBHOOK_URL` are what leave the pod (`NTH: pkg/webhook/webhook.go:83`, `:103-112`, `:115`).

The content is parsed with `text/template`, not `html/template`, and given `sprig.TxtFuncMap()` (`NTH: pkg/webhook/webhook.go:58`, `:149`). Its data is one `combinedDrainData` value: the node metadata, the interruption event, the instance ID and the instance type (`:33-38`, `:74`). A file containing no `{{ }}` action parses and executes unchanged, so its bytes become the POST body. What the sprig function set itself can address is outside the tree and is carried as unsettled.

Startup validation is not a path restriction. `ValidateWebhookConfig` returns nil at once when `WEBHOOK_URL` is empty (`NTH: pkg/webhook/webhook.go:133-135`); otherwise it reads the same file, parses it and executes it against an empty `combinedDrainData` (`:140`, `:149`, `:155`). A file with no template actions passes. A read failure is fatal at startup (`NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:107-111`) but only logged at post time (`NTH: pkg/webhook/webhook.go:46-51`).

The pod's service-account token path under the shipped chart is not stated in the chart. The chart sets `serviceAccountName` (posture, `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/templates/deployment.yaml:35`) and never sets `automountServiceAccountToken`, so the Kubernetes default mount applies (inferred, seam: admission and the kubelet). The path itself is inferred, not cited from the tree, and is carried as unsettled.

The boundary that sets the variable is B2. It is `--webhook-template-file` or the `WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_FILE` environment variable (`NTH: pkg/config/config.go:54`, `:218`). The chart sets it only to `/config/<key>` from a named ConfigMap (posture, `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/templates/deployment.yaml:144-146`; `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/templates/daemonset.linux.yaml:139-141`), so an arbitrary path arrives through `extraEnv` (posture, `templates/deployment.yaml:179-181`) or through a deployment that does not use the chart.

## Part B-PG: Cross-package findings from the Postgres-HA packages, in STRIDE

Every seam row from the three pairwise models, plus the rows the Percona-joined, Zalando-joined and
Vault-only chains establish, aggregated into six STRIDE subsections. The pairwise-model OP rows carry an explicit
STRIDE tag and it is used; OP-X14, the negative-fact row the clock seam adds, carries none and is categorized by its subsection and its mechanism, stated in the Evidence column. KB, KP, PC, ZA and VA rows carry no tag; each is categorized by its
mechanism, stated in the Evidence column. Columns:
`| ID | Packages | Actor | Entry | Evidence | Gap | Halt on fault |`. Gap is the failed
property number.

## Part C: Chains

The grouping and ordering rule follows each source aggregate. Group J, the chains that cross between the node-and-host stack and the Postgres-HA stack, opens Part C. The groups from the node-and-host aggregate (M, NK, N, K, X, HS, AS, H, A) follow in that order, then the groups from the Postgres-HA aggregate (KB, KP, OP, RG, AG, PC, ZA, VA) in that order. Every chain is carried in its source's shape, ids and titles kept; a `**At the new seam.**` line is added after any chain a verified new seam touches.

### Group J: chains that cross between the node-and-host stack and the Postgres-HA stack

No cross-aggregate chain survives any of the three seams between the node-and-host stack and the Postgres-HA stack. Each seam was walked in both directions, from the node-and-host stack toward the Postgres-HA stack and back, in every deployment mode the two aggregates carry (NTH IMDS and Queue Processor, both node-drain surfaces, the Percona-operated, Zalando-operated and bare-daemon deployments, and `ha_enabled` on and off), and each was checked independently against the crossing rule, that a chain joins a gap on one side to a gap on the other so the combined impact exceeds what either reaches alone; none kept a chain. The clock seam keeps no chain because every HA-critical Postgres-HA timer is monotonic (keepalived's scheduler at `KA: lib/timer.c:119-159` and `KA: lib/scheduler.c:808`, Patroni's leader hold at `PT: ha.py:298`, `:309`) or evaluated by the database server's `NOW()` (`OB: internal/physical/postgresql/postgresql.go:239`, `:252-255`; `VA: physical/postgresql/postgresql.go:189`, `:196-197`), so chronyd disciplining the host moves no election or lock decision. The node-lifecycle seam keeps no chain because neither the termination handler nor the node drain reads any Patroni, OpenBao or operator application signal and the placed pods hold their data on PVCs the drain's `emptyDir`-only destruction never reaches (`KD: pkg/drain/filters.go:164-172`, `:221-228`; `ZA: pkg/cluster/k8sres.go:1551`; `PC: percona/controller/pgcluster/finalizer.go:24-47`), so a consumer acting on the pod list, the eviction response or the cordon bit is obeying, not exhibiting a gap. The credentials-and-commands seam keeps no chain because the EKS exec credential authenticates only to the Kubernetes API server while Patroni's `check_access` and both operators authenticate in-cluster (`PT: api.py:1715-1749`; `PC: internal/controller/runtime/runtime.go:46-48`; `ZA: pkg/util/k8sutil/k8sutil.go:125-131`), and OpenBao mounts no AWS auth method or secrets engine (`OB: internal/builtin/credential/`, `OB: internal/builtin/logical/`), so the named "OpenBao issuing or consuming AWS credentials" edge does not exist in the tree. Two Postgres-HA-side rows record the clock split as negative facts, OP-X14 and VA-X3; no other row and no chain crosses. The candidates tested and rejected at each seam are in Part C2, and what each seam closes is in Part E.

### Group M: chains that cross between the node lifecycle and the host's clock and credentials

The edge in all three is the host clock. chronyd writes it through the kernel; the handler and the drain read it through the Go runtime. That the clock chronyd sets is the clock either consumer reads is inferred, seam: the kernel and the Go runtime, and keeps that marking at every use. `HOST-CLOCK` is the entry term for the kernel clock as chronyd leaves it, read through the Go runtime. M1 and M2 cross between chrony and the termination handler; M3 crosses between chrony and the node drain.

#### M1. A host clock behind the queue's time by more than the grace period holds each queue event built from the message's `time` as future, and past its instance's end once the lag also exceeds the instance's remaining time, while the send time the handler requests on every message goes unread (source-supported; Queue Processor mode)

**Packages and edges crossed.** chrony's reference and slew engine, its step path, its source-loss path or its fatal-exit path; the kernel clock; the handler's event-store gate and the queue message's `time`. One edge, the host clock, from chronyd to the handler; every crossing of it is inferred, seam: the kernel and the Go runtime.

**Entry points.**
- One branch, `NTP-RESP`, B3: an accepted offset that puts the host clock behind, slewed at the tree default, with `makestep` and `maxchange` off (`CH-C1`; `CH: conf.c:152-153`, `:163`; `CH: reference.c:544-545`, `:557-558`, `:1053-1064`). Reach bounded by the slew clamp (`CH: sys_generic.c:219-223`; `CH: conf.c:104`; `CH-T7`).
- One branch, `CMDMON`, B2: a backward step through the command socket, which checks only the address family (`CH-T1`; `CH: cmdmon.c:1116-1121`, `:1494-1499`; `CH: local.c:690-710`; `CH: sys_linux.c:104-120`).
- One branch, `NONE`: a clock free-running on its last frequency after every source is lost, with the reference still claiming synchronisation (`CH-C2`; `CH: sources.c:1000-1007`), or a stranded correction frequency after a fatal exit (`CH-C3`; `CH: logging.c:170-183`; `CH: sys_generic.c:430-447`).
- The reader, `SQS`, no actor: a genuine queue message whose `time` is the event's own time (posture, `NTH: README.md:327-342`).

**Steps.**
1. chronyd leaves the kernel clock behind the queue's time by more than `NODE_TERMINATION_GRACE_PERIOD` seconds through one entry branch. Source-supported within chronyd (`CH: reference.c:1053-1064`; `CH: local.c:702-705`; `CH: sys_generic.c:238`, `:266-270`); the kernel time and the handler's read of it are inferred, seam: the kernel and the Go runtime.
2. The queue monitor receives up to ten messages with the `SentTimestamp` system attribute requested (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:306-317`, `:307-309`). The spot interruption, rebalance, state-change and Auto Scaling termination builders each receive the `*sqs.Message` and set `StartTime` from the message's `time`, or from now when it does not parse; the launch builder does the same (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/asg-lifecycle-event.go:279`, `:308`), and the scheduled-change builder sets `StartTime` to now (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/scheduled-change-event.go:101`) and is outside this chain (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/event-bridge.go:36-43`; `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/spot-itn-event.go:51`, `:67`; `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/rebalance-recommendation-event.go:49`, `:65`; `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/ec2-state-change-event.go:53`, `:72`; `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/asg-lifecycle-event.go:71`, `:92`). The attribute is read nowhere: a search over every non-test `.go` file under `NTH: cmd/` and `NTH: pkg/` for `Attributes` and `SentTimestamp` returns the request and no read of a message attribute; its other hits are OpenTelemetry `WithAttributes` calls that read no message (`NTH: pkg/observability/opentelemetry.go:131`, `:150-151`). Source-supported (negative). That the service returns the attribute is inferred, seam: SQS.
3. The store admits the event, and the gate holds it while `time.Until(StartTime - grace)` is positive, read from the wall clock; the main loop dispatches only when it is at or below zero (`NTH: pkg/interruptioneventstore/interruption-event-store.go:64-79`, `:107-119`; `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:285-306`; `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:41-42`, `:211`; posture `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/values.yaml:106`). With the clock behind by more than the grace period, `time.Until` is positive at receipt for an event whose `time` is the present, and stays positive until the lag less the grace period has elapsed on the local clock. Source-supported; that `time.Until` against a parsed timestamp reads the wall clock is inferred, seam: the Go runtime.
4. While the event waits the message is not deleted, because deletion is the post-drain task (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/spot-itn-event.go:75-81`; `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/ec2-state-change-event.go:82-88`; `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/asg-lifecycle-event.go:110-113`); it returns after the visibility timeout (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:301-304`, `:315`; `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:126`) and is dropped as a duplicate on every re-receipt (`NTH: pkg/interruptioneventstore/interruption-event-store.go:66-69`), as `N-T5` records for a far-future time. Source-supported.
5. The instance ends on its own schedule: a spot interruption after its notice, an Auto Scaling termination when the hook's timeout expires, a state change already under way. Inferred, seam: EC2 and EC2 Auto Scaling (posture, `NTH: README.md:93-99`). Distance 0 needs the lag to exceed the grace period plus that remaining time.
6. When the gate opens, the handler cordons and calls the drain with `Timeout` set to the same grace period (`NTH: pkg/node/node.go:132`, `:171`, `:752`; `KD: pkg/drain/drain.go:271-278`), after the instance has ended; that the timeout runs on the monotonic clock is inferred, seam: the Go runtime. A node object already removed makes the label read a Warn (`NTH: pkg/interruptionevent/draincordon/handler.go:71-78`) and the cordon a not-found, logged at `:169-170` with no metric and no event; with `TAINT_NODE` at its default false (code `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:231`; chart, posture `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/values.yaml:87`; they agree), the event is cancelled (`NTH: pkg/interruptionevent/draincordon/handler.go:124-128`) and `HandleEvent` returns nil (`:145`). With `TAINT_NODE` true, a spot interruption's pre-drain taint fails first (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/spot-itn-event.go:95-99`), and the handler cancels the event and returns the error (`NTH: pkg/interruptionevent/draincordon/handler.go:84-94`), which is logged at `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:382-385`. Whether the node object still exists is inferred, seam: the Kubernetes node lifecycle controller.

**Seams crossed.** chronyd's reference, step path, loss path or stranded slew to the kernel clock; the kernel clock to the handler's `time.Until` (`NTH: pkg/interruptioneventstore/interruption-event-store.go:119`; seam: the kernel and the Go runtime); the gate to the main loop's dispatch (`NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:292-299`); the process to EC2 and EC2 Auto Scaling.

**Combined impact.** Distance 0 by omission where the lag exceeds the grace period plus the instance's remaining time: the instance ends with its pods placed while the drain that would have moved them waits in the store. Below that sum the drain starts late inside the instance's life, which shifts NK1 step 7's alignment and adds no outcome. The rebalance builder's event has no instance end, and the launch builder's event reaches the launch path, not a drain. Halt: none on either side. Records: chronyd's WARN once above `logchange` (`CH: reference.c:498-499`) or at a step (`CH: local.c:707`), or CRIT on the fatal branch, to syslog, which the handler does not read; the handler's Info "Adding new event to the event store" with the event's `StartTime` (`NTH: pkg/interruptioneventstore/interruption-event-store.go:74`) and the periodic store line with a drainable count (`:188-206`), neither naming a deferral. chronyd's gap alone leaves a wrong clock. The handler's gate alone, under a correct clock, dispatches at once for every builder that uses the message's `time`. Joined, the gate treats a present event as future for as long as the lag exceeds the grace period, and the one value the handler's tree requests that could have shown the lag (what the vendored SDK reads from a response is inferred, seam: the AWS SDK for Go), the queue's send time, is requested on every receive and never read. Configuration: Queue Processor mode, `ENABLE_SQS_TERMINATION_DRAINING=true` with `QUEUE_URL` set (code default false, `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:62-63`; chart default false, posture `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/values.yaml:141`; they agree); `NODE_TERMINATION_GRACE_PERIOD` 120 at both defaults, which agree. Live at those defaults through the `NTP-RESP` and `NONE` branches with no B2 act.

**Composition.** `CH-C1` or `CH-T1` or `CH-C2` or `CH-C3`, with `CH-T7` for the slew's reach, joined to the store's gate, carried as new row `N-D15`, with `N-T5` for the held message and NK1 step 7 for the aligned timeout. Chrony-side gap: no bound on an accepted offset at the tree default (`CH: conf.c:152-153`, `:163`), a socket that checks nothing about the requester (`CH: cmdmon.c:1494-1499`), a reference that keeps its claim after loss (`CH: sources.c:1000-1007`), or a finalise that runs on the clean path only (`CH: sys_generic.c:430-447`). Handler-side gap: the gate schedules the drain from the wall clock against a server-issued time while each builder holds the message carrying the queue's own send time, requested at `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:307-309` and read nowhere; a check omitted at the line with the value in scope, not a reporting channel. Not a duplicate: `N-T5` needs a B2 sender supplying a future `time`, NK1 needs a hung call. In IMDS mode the same gate with a metadata-service `time` is obedience (Part C2, chrony against the termination handler and the node drain, item 1).

#### M2. A forward step of the host clock through chronyd, between the handler's own reboot label and its next start, is read as a reboot: the node is uncordoned, its taints removed when `TAINT_NODE` is set, and the scheduled event ignored, so the maintenance lands with new pods placed (source-supported; IMDS mode)

**Packages and edges crossed.** chrony's command channel and step path; the kernel wall clock and the kernel's boot-relative reading; the handler's reboot label write, its startup reboot check, its uncordon, its label and taint removal and its ignore set. One edge, the host clock, from chronyd to the handler, inferred at the kernel and the Go runtime.

- One branch, `CONFIG`, B2: a `makestep` directive in the distribution configuration (off in the tree, `CH: conf.c:152-153`), which steps while its limit lasts from chronyd's start, or always under a negative limit (`CH: reference.c:542-550`), so a chronyd restart with no host reboot reaches it; deployment assumption, recorded not scored.
- The reader, `IMDS`, no actor: a restart-class scheduled event, `instance-stop`, `system-reboot`, `instance-reboot` or `instance-retirement`, on a schedulable node, which is what writes the label (`NTH: pkg/monitor/scheduledevent/scheduled-event-monitor.go:32-35`, `:87-88`, `:150-155`; `NTH: pkg/node/node.go:281-299`).

**Steps.**
1. On a restart-class scheduled event the pre-drain task marks the node with the event ID, taints it when `TAINT_NODE` is set (`NTH: pkg/monitor/scheduledevent/scheduled-event-monitor.go:124-127`; `NTH: pkg/node/node.go:532-535`; code default false, `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:231`; chart default false, posture `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/values.yaml:87`; they agree), and, when the node is not already unschedulable, writes `action=UncordonAfterReboot` and `action-time` set to `time.Now().Unix()`. The event's `StartTime` is now, so the drain follows at once (`N-D11`) and the label sits on the node for the lead time to `NotBefore`. Source-supported: `NTH: pkg/monitor/scheduledevent/scheduled-event-monitor.go:109`, `:117-143`; `NTH: pkg/node/node.go:283`, `:288`. That `Unix()` returns the wall-clock reading is inferred, seam: the Go runtime.

On Linux every slew is a frequency and tick write, because the driver is registered with no accrue-offset driver (`CH: sys_linux.c:394-398`; `CH: sys_generic.c:227-238`; `CH: sys_linux.c:156-160`); a frequency write moves the wall clock and the boot-relative reading alike and a set-offset moves the wall clock alone (inferred, seam: the kernel), so the slew branches `CH-C1`, `CH-C3` and `CH-T7` cannot reach this step.

The handler process starts on that node in IMDS mode with `ENABLE_SCHEDULED_EVENT_DRAINING` on (code default true, `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:56-57`; chart default true, posture `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/values.yaml:280`; the DaemonSet hardcodes the mode, posture `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/templates/daemonset.linux.yaml:156-157`). Source-supported: `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:171-186`, `:312-330`.

The event ID is added to the ignore set, so the same scheduled event, which the metadata monitor re-reads every 2 s while it is pending, is admitted to the store with an Info line and is never drainable for the life of the process. Source-supported: `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:251`, `:328`; `NTH: pkg/interruptioneventstore/interruption-event-store.go:74`, `:107-109`, `:135-142`.

**Seams crossed.** chronyd's command channel (`CH: cmdmon.c:1116-1121`) to the step path (`CH: local.c:691-709`) to the kernel wall clock; the kernel wall clock and the boot-relative reading to the handler's one comparison of them (`NTH: pkg/node/node.go:614`, `:621`; seam: the kernel and the Go runtime); the comparison to the uncordon, the label and taint removal and the ignore set (`:625-634`; `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:328`).

### Group NK: chains that cross the boundary between the termination handler and the node drain

### Group N: chains inside the termination handler

#### N1. A drain with no deadline runs under a constant liveness answer until the instance ends beneath it (source-supported)

**Risk and impact.** No actor is needed. Every Kubernetes call in the drain and taint path opens at `context.TODO()` with no deadline, so a call that never returns holds a worker for the life of the process. The main loop dispatches and forgets, consulting the wait group only at shutdown, so ten held workers stop all dispatch with one warning per second and nothing else. Throughout, the liveness probe answers a constant 200 and the Auto Scaling lifecycle heartbeat, when configured, keeps beating, so every observer outside the process reads the handler as healthy. In IMDS mode EC2 ends the instance on its own schedule with the pods still placed (inferred, seam: EC2). In Queue Processor mode the beat holds the instance in wait while the drain that justifies the hold is wedged (inferred, seam: EC2 Auto Scaling). If SIGTERM arrives first, the main loop waits on the in-flight handler with no deadline and the container is killed at the end of the grace period with the eviction half done (inferred, seam: the kubelet). The workload's data goes with the instance, and no recorder in the tree says a drain failed.

**Entry points.**
- The reader, NONE, `NONE`, the drain executor and the main loop. Source-supported. A wedged Kubernetes call, from a slow API server, a stuck eviction or a pod that will not terminate, needs no actor and no privileged act.

#### N2. Two self-signals that read no state both survive the executor's wedge and misreport it (source-supported)

**Risk and impact.** No actor is needed. The two signals meant to report the handler's own health, the Auto Scaling lifecycle heartbeat and the liveness probe, both read no state. When a drain wedges, the beat keeps telling the Auto Scaling group to hold the instance and the probe keeps telling the kubelet the pod is healthy, so the failure they exist to report is the failure they conceal. When the process panics instead, both signals stop, by the process dying rather than by either signal detecting anything. The dead-man's switch the model requires is inverted: observation does not gate execution, execution emits observation about itself.

**Entry points.**
- The reader, NONE, `NONE`, the heartbeat sender and the liveness handler. Source-supported. A wedge or a panic needs no actor. Position: inside the process the signals claim to describe.

2. What the beat gates is destruction of the instance by the Auto Scaling group. When it stops, destruction proceeds (inferred, seam: EC2 Auto Scaling), so the beat holds the instance while the drain is wedged and releases it when the executor dies, when `HeartbeatUntil` passes, or when a beat is refused with `ValidationError`. Source-supported on the emit and on the stops (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/asg-lifecycle-event.go:190`, `:209-212`, `:214-220`, `:244-246`). Inferred (EC2 Auto Scaling) on the hold; posture `NTH: README.md:93-95`, `:99`.

4. On the duplicate-error panic the whole process exits, so both signals stop together, by death, not detection. Source-supported: `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:263-266`.

#### N3. One queue message drains any managed node with no source, account or resource check (source-supported)

**Risk and impact.** A principal that can place a message on the queue reaches a drain of any managed node in the cluster through the handler's own service account, which holds node patch and update and pod eviction on every node. The classifier checks the source and detail-type strings and the state field, and reads the account, region and resources fields nowhere. Nothing ties a message to this cluster except the instance's managed tag, which the sender satisfies by naming a real tagged instance. The drain runs with force and empty-dir deletion on, and the message is deleted on success, so no trace remains on the queue.

**Entry points.**
- Required, B2, `SQS`, the queue producer boundary. Source-supported. Position: the message body, before any check in the tree runs.

**Every check it passes.** The body parses as JSON (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:125`). If `detail-type` is empty, the body must parse as a lifecycle message and `LifecycleTransition` must equal one of two exact strings (`:168`, `:181-183`). `source` must be one of three exact service strings, and for two of them `detail-type` must be one of four exact strings (`:206-239`). For a state change, `strings.Contains` on the state (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/ec2-state-change-event.go:60`). For AWS Health, the service and event-category fields must each equal one fixed value (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/scheduled-change-event.go:78-86`). `detail.instance-id` must resolve through `DescribeInstances` under the handler's own credentials with a non-empty `PrivateDnsName` (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:365`, `:395-416`). With `CHECK_TAG_BEFORE_DRAINING` at its default the instance must carry `ManagedTag` (`:438-442`, `:266-269`; `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:70-71`, `:226`, `:228`).

**Every check that does not exist.** `account`, `region` and `resources` are declared at `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/event-bridge.go:29`, `:31`, `:32` and read nowhere in the repository. No ARN is parsed. No signature, message attribute or sender identity is examined anywhere in `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/`. Nothing ties the message to this cluster beyond the instance tag. `instance-action` on the spot path is declared and never read. The lifecycle action token is not read before the drain except by the heartbeat goroutine, and never validated in the tree. No allow-list of nodes exists, and no second source is consulted about whether the named instance is really ending.

**What the actor needs.** The ability to place a message on that queue, a B2 position. The documented queue policy names only the service principals `events.amazonaws.com` and `sqs.amazonaws.com` (posture, `NTH: README.md:334-337`), so the position is not granted by that policy; which other principals hold send rights is set outside the tree (inferred, seam: SQS and IAM).

**What the node loses.** The node is cordoned (`NTH: pkg/node/node.go:180-194`), then every pod on it is evicted or deleted except three classes the drain helper excludes: pods whose controller owner reference is a DaemonSet that exists and whose phase is neither `Succeeded` nor `Failed`, since `IgnoreAllDaemonSets` is on by default (`NTH: pkg/node/node.go:749`; `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:205`; `KD: pkg/drain/filters.go:181-188`, `:199-203`); pods carrying the mirror-pod annotation key, whatever its value (`KD: pkg/drain/filters.go:207-208`); and the handler's own pod, matched on `POD_NAME` and `NAMESPACE` (`NTH: pkg/node/node.go:750`, `:925-932`), where `POD_NAME` is empty at the code default (`NTH: pkg/config/config.go:202`) and set from the downward API by the chart (posture, `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/templates/deployment.yaml:63-66`), so outside the chart that filter matches no pod (`N-T8`). A DaemonSet-owned pod in `Succeeded` or `Failed` is not excluded; it is evicted (`KD: pkg/drain/filters.go:186-188`). A DaemonSet-owned pod whose DaemonSet lookup fails with anything other than not-found halts the whole node before any write (`KD: pkg/drain/filters.go:190`, `:196`; `KD: pkg/drain/drain.go:209-211`). `Force: true` means pods no controller owns are admitted to the write list with a warning rather than halting the node (`NTH: pkg/node/node.go:747`; `KD: pkg/drain/filters.go:241-242`). #### N4. An empty-state message drains a healthy node that the Queue Processor can never uncordon (source-supported)

**Risk and impact.** A message with an empty or partial state field drains and cordons a healthy node in Queue Processor mode, and nothing in the tree ever reverses it. After the drain the store marks every event for the node processed but keeps the event until a periodic cleanup, so the same message on redelivery is dropped as a duplicate. The one uncordon path in the process is driven by a channel only the IMDS scheduled-event monitor writes, and the other is gated on IMDS mode at startup, so in Queue Processor mode neither fires; even if the cancel watcher did, the still-present processed event pins its uncordon gate to false. The cordon and the eviction persist for the life of the node.

#### N6. One poison message crash-loops the single Queue Processor for the whole cluster (source-supported)

**Risk and impact.** In Queue Processor mode one Deployment pod serves the entire cluster, and a single message it cannot process ends the process. A message alone on the queue that fails to parse, names an unsupported source, or names a running instance with an empty private DNS name raises a constant error on every receive that delivers it. The supervisor counts identical error strings and panics on the fourth, ending every goroutine, including in-flight drains and heartbeat senders. The message returns after the visibility timeout and the fault recurs at each restart, so all cluster-wide drain processing crash-loops. Nothing else in the cluster is doing that work, so while the loop runs, nodes whose instances are ending are not drained. The only records are log lines, an Error line per failed message, a Warn line per monitor error and the Warn that precedes the panic, and a process exit, with Kubernetes events and Prometheus metrics off by default (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:101`, `:110`; `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:254`, `:264`; `NTH: pkg/logging/versioned.go:30`).

**Entry points.**
- One cause, B2 or NONE, `SQS`, the queue producer boundary or a transport fault. Source-supported. Position: the message body, or the transport beneath the receive call.

**Steps.**
1. A message that fails to parse, names an unsupported source, or names a running instance with an empty private DNS name is counted as a failed message (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:102`, `:111`), and the batch fails only when every message in it fails (`:115`). When it is the only message on the queue, the constant error `none of the waiting queue events could be processed` is returned on every receive that delivers it, and a receive that delivers no message returns nil. Source-supported: `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:96-105`, `:115-117`, `:241-242`, `:405-416`.
2. The supervisor increments on each identical error string and panics on the fourth; the error text is a constant, so the count always reaches the threshold of 3 tested with `>=`. The counter and the previous-error string live per monitor goroutine and are written only inside the error branch, so a tick that returns no error resets neither, and the four identical errors need not be consecutive. The message is not deleted, and a receive while it is hidden returns no message and no error (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:115-117`), so the four identical errors are spaced by the message's returns, not by the tick; the return is inferred, seam: Amazon SQS. Source-supported: `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:249-250`, `:251`, `:253`, `:258`, `:260-261`, `:257-266`, `:62`; `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:116`.
3. The Deployment ships one replica, so the panic stops all cluster-wide processing. The undeleted message returns after the visibility timeout, default 20 s, and the fault recurs at each restart. Source-supported: `NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:301-316`; `NTH: pkg/config/config.go:125-126`. Posture: `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/values.yaml:147-148`; `NTH: config/helm/aws-node-termination-handler/templates/deployment.yaml:10`. Restart inferred (kubelet); the chart sets no `restartPolicy`. The message's return after the visibility timeout the receive requests is inferred, seam: SQS.

**Seam crossed.** The queue producer boundary to the single processor's liveness, and the kubelet outside the system that restarts the pod into the same fault with the same configuration.

**Combined impact.** Distance to the workload's data is by omission: while the processor crash-loops, no node is drained before its instance ends, so workloads on ending instances lose their data. Halt: full, process exit, `N-H4` feeding `N-H3`, reaching zero observers inside the system. Configuration: `ENABLE_SQS_TERMINATION_DRAINING=true` with `QUEUE_URL`, plus `replicas: 1`, the chart default; code and chart defaults agree on the mode flag.

**Composition.** `N-H4`, `N-H3`, `N-D2`, `N-D3`.

### Group K: chains inside the node drain

Distance scale for the node drain: Distance 0, the tree's own write or omission destroys the workload's pod or its `emptyDir` data, or leaves the pod on a node the caller has been told is drained. Distance 1, one act outside the tree stands between the chain and that outcome. Distance 2, the outcome is a wrong or lost record only.

### Group X: the chain that crosses chrony, the CLI and the agent

#### X1. A host clock past both the agent's token expiry and the instance credential's stated expiry: the agent's recurring write windows hand a script to the instance profile role, and the CLI's expiry rewrite defeats the still-expired halt that would have stopped it (deployment assumption: the service's acceptance of requests signed by that clock, and the two service-issued lifetimes, seams; no configuration)

**Packages and edges.** chrony's reference and slew engine, its step path or its fatal-exit path; the kernel clock, read by the agent's rotation scheduler and by the CLI's instance-credential fetcher and credential object; the agent's store and runtime-config writes and the script hand-off; the CLI's resolver. Two edges: the host clock, from chronyd to both consumers, and the credential hand-off across the shared credentials file and `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE`, from the agent to the CLI.

**Preconditions.** As `SSM-E1`: EC2 identity, with the Systems Manager source and an instance profile attached. That combination means either the attached role is one Systems Manager refuses with `AccessDeniedException` or `AssumeRoleUnauthorizedAccess`, or the metadata service did not return its credentials at the last retrieve (`SSM: common/identity/credentialproviders/ec2roleprovider/ec2_role_provider.go:134-148`; `SSM: common/identity/credentialproviders/ec2roleprovider/ec2_role_provider_deps.go:41-45`). The metadata service returns a four-field credential to the CLI (inferred, seam: IMDS). The script makes an unnamed CLI run. As `HS2`: the host clock is at or past the stored token expiry. Beyond `HS2`: the host clock is at or past the stated `Expiration` of the instance credential the metadata service returns. How far ahead that is, compared with the offset `HS2` needs, is decided by the two service-issued lifetimes (inferred, seams: AWS-API and IMDS). No configuration away from any tree's default.

**Entry points.**
- One branch, `NTP-RESP`, B3: an accepted offset that puts the host clock ahead, as `HS2` (`CH-C1`; `CH: conf.c:152-153`; `CH: reference.c:1053-1064`). Reach is bounded by the slew rate at the tree default.
- One branch, `NONE`: a stranded correction frequency after a fatal exit, as `HS2` (`CH-C3`; `CH: sys_generic.c:430-447`; `CH: logging.c:170-183`).
- One branch, `CMDMON`, B2: a step as `HS1`, which steps by the remaining correction (`CH: cmdmon.c:1116-1121`; `CH: local.c:690-710`). That correction's cause is `NTP-RESP`, B3.
- The windows, `HOST-CLOCK` and `NONE`: the recurring store and runtime-config writes (`SSM-D13`), with no actor once the clock is past the stored expiry.
- Required, `SCRIPT-ENV`, B2: a document whose script makes an unnamed `aws` call started inside a store window (`SSM-T2`) or a runtime-config write (`SSM-E8`). This is `SSM-E1`'s entry.
- `IMDS`: the metadata service's own answer, with no actor (`CLI-T3`'s entry).

**Steps.**
1. chronyd leaves the kernel clock ahead through one of the entry branches, as `HS2` step 1. Source-supported within chronyd. The kernel time, and each consumer's read of it, are inferred, seam: the kernel and the Go and Python runtimes.
2. The agent's rotation delay is zero on every pass while the stored expiry is at or before the host clock (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:136-137`). Each successful pass on the Systems Manager source stores the share file by loading it and saving it back, and the save truncates on write (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:414-424`; `SSM: agent/managedInstances/sharedCredentials/shared_Credentials.go:84, 103`; seam `SSM: vendor/gopkg.in/ini.v1/file.go:511`). The pass then rewrites the runtime config (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:435-447`), storing the returned expiry untested at `:438`. These are `HS2` steps 3 to 5 (`SSM-D13`). Source-supported; each pass's retrieve being accepted is inferred, seam: AWS-API.
3. A script started inside a window gets `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` pointing at an empty or partial file. If its runtime-config read fails, it gets no credential variables at all (`SSM: agent/plugins/runscript/runscript.go:100-112`; `ShareFile` is set only for the Systems Manager source, `SSM: common/identity/credentialproviders/ec2roleprovider/ec2_role_provider.go:224-231`). Source-supported; the truncate and the decode failure are inferred, seam: the Go standard library.
4. The CLI's shared-file provider finds no `default` keys and returns `None` (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:1379-1385`). The chain falls through to the instance-metadata provider (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:135-150, 2231-2243`), which loads the instance role (`:1150-1177`). This is `SSM-E1`, the CLI doing what the empty file or the missing variable directs. It is also the edge into the rewrite. Outside a window, the same run resolves from the share file to a `Credentials` object with no expiry (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:1397`) and never reaches the fetcher. The substitution is what places this run's credential on the fetcher's path. Source-supported.
5. The fetcher calls `_evaluate_expiration` before returning (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:551`). With the host clock at or past the stated expiry minus the window, it replaces the expiry with now plus 1020 to 1500 s and keeps no copy of the service value (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:630-645`). This is `A1` (`CLI-T3`, `CLI-E9`). Source-supported.
6. The credential object is built from the rewritten value (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:458, 1172-1176`). Its remaining time exceeds the 900 s advisory window, so `_refresh` returns at `:564-565` and the still-expired check at `:616` never runs. If the service value had been kept, a host clock at or past the stated expiry would take the mandatory refresh (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:564-588`) and refetch (`:590-612`). It would then raise `RuntimeError` at `CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:627`, which is the CLI's halt path 2. That holds whether the metadata service returned the same credential or a new one stated to expire before the host clock (the latter inferred, seam: IMDS). The rewrite defeats the one halt on the substituted path. Source-supported.
7. The run signs as the instance profile role, with a signing timestamp from the same clock (seam extension `CLI: awscli/botocore/auth.py:429`). Whether the target services accept it is inferred, seam: AWS-API.

**Seams crossed.** Four crossings, then the services:
- chronyd's reference, step path or stranded slew to the kernel clock (`CH: reference.c:1064`; `CH: local.c:702-705`; `CH: sys_generic.c:238, 266-270`).
- The kernel clock to the agent's `getCurrentTimeFunc` (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:132`), to the CLI's `utcnow()` in the fetcher (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:636`) and to the credential object's time read (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:519`). Seam: the kernel, the Go runtime, the Python runtime.
- The zero delay to the store and config writes, and the window to the script's environment (`SSM: agent/plugins/runscript/runscript.go:100-112`).
- The file and `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` to the CLI's resolver, and the resolver to the fetcher's rewrite and the credential object's still-expired check.
- Then the process to the metadata service and the target services (seams: IMDS, AWS-API).

**Combined impact.** Distance 0. A script's unnamed `aws` call signs as the instance profile role in place of the default-host-management role, with no halt. This happens on a host whose clock is at or past both the agent's stored token expiry and the instance credential's stated expiry.
- `HS2`'s gaps alone, with the CLI keeping the service value, bring the substituted run over that range to the CLI's halt path 2: `RuntimeError` at `CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:627`, a stop that fails closed.
- `A1` alone, with no substitution, rewrites only the credential of a run that reached the instance role with no substitution, and that run's keys are the right principal's (Part C2, chrony and the CLI, first row). A script on a host using the Systems Manager source never reaches the fetcher outside a window.
- Joined, the rewrite lifts the halt that would have stopped the substitution, and the recurring windows feed runs to it on every pass.
- Below that range, where the clock is past the token expiry but short of the instance credential's stated expiry, `HS2` reaches the substitution without `A1`, and this chain adds nothing.

The keys signed are the ones the metadata service issued. Keys past their stated expiry by the service's own clock remain `A1`'s own seam (IMDS), not a reach of this chain. Which role carries more permission is set by IAM (seam). Halt: none; the CLI's halt path 2 is defeated.

Records:
- The agent writes no rotation-time line in this state: the zero delay returns at `SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:136-137` before the Info at `:151`. Each pass writes Info "Credentials ready" (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:208`, reached from `:450`), and on EC2 the provider writes a Warn at the refused instance-profile attempt and an Info "Successfully connected with Systems Manager role credentials" (`SSM: common/identity/credentialproviders/ec2roleprovider/ec2_role_provider.go:139, 156`).
- chronyd writes WARN once above 1 s (`CH: reference.c:498-499`) or at a step (`CH: local.c:707`), or CRIT once on the fatal-exit branch, to syslog, which neither consumer reads.
- The CLI writes `INFO` at `CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:646-651`, which a default run discards (`CLI: awscli/botocore/__init__.py:28-29`; `CLI: awscli/clidriver.py:657-660`). The `WARNING` at `CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:626` is never reached.

Reach: each pass's retrieve being accepted (AWS-API) and the two service-issued lifetimes (AWS-API, IMDS) are inferred. Because these steps rest on seams no tree settles, the chain is a deployment assumption without a configuration.

**Composition.** `CH-C1` or `CH-C3` or `CH-T1`, joined to `SSM-D13` with `SSM-T2`, `SSM-E8` and `SSM-E1` (chain `HS2`), joined along the credential hand-off to `CLI-T3` + `CLI-E9` + `CLI-R3` and the CLI's halt path 2 (chain `A1`). Chrony-side gap: as `HS2`. Agent-side gap: as `HS2` (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:136-137, 438`). CLI-side gap: the fetcher's rewrite keeps no copy of the service value, so it defeats the still-expired halt (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:640-645`; `CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:616-627`). The CLI's fall-through to the instance role is obedience to the file or environment the agent left, as `SSM-E1` records, not a further gap. Not a duplicate, for three reasons. `HS2` carries the CLI resolution as `SSM-E1`'s finding and does not name the halt the rewrite defeats. `A1`, with its closure on a clock ahead, keeps the right principal. No Part C2 row joins the three.

### Group HS: chains that cross between chrony and the agent

Source-supported except the driver write to the kernel, inferred, seam: the kernel.
2. The kernel clock moves forward by the step; the agent's `time.Now()` returns the moved clock. Inferred, seam: the kernel and the Go runtime.
3. Each persisted failed reply carries its persist time in its file name from the host clock at persist: MGS `SSM: agent/messageservice/interactor/mgsinteractor/sendreply.go:304-305` (source-supported); MDS writer `SSM: agent/runcommand/mds/service.go:334-335` (seam, opened only to confirm that the name carries the persist time). **Seam crossed.** chronyd's command channel (`CH: cmdmon.c:1116-1121`) to the step path (`CH: local.c:691-709`) to the kernel clock; the kernel clock to the agent's wall-clock read (`SSM: agent/messageservice/utils/messageutil.go:296`; seam: the kernel and the Go runtime); the validity check to the MDS pass delete (`SSM: agent/messageservice/interactor/mdsinteractor/mdsinteractor.go:627-630`).

Reach: step 4 is inferred, seam: AWS-API; because that step rests on a seam no tree settles, the chain is a deployment assumption without a configuration. Where the host clock is also at or past the stated expiry of the instance credential the metadata service returns, the substituted run signs only because the CLI's expiry rewrite defeats its still-expired halt (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:640-645`; `CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:616-627`); that join is X1.

**Composition.** `CH-C1` or `CH-C3` or `CH-T1`, joined to the success branch of the agent's continue-on-fault path for a failed credential retrieve and to `SSM-T2`, `SSM-E8`, `SSM-E1`, `SSM-I5`, carried as new row `SSM-D13`. Chrony-side gap: no bound on an accepted offset at the tree default (`CH: conf.c:152-153`) or no end to a stranded correction (`CH: sys_generic.c:430-447` runs on the clean path only). Agent-side gap: `durationUntilRefresh` reads a stored expiry at or before the host clock as "rotate now" with no floor, and the loop stores a returned expiry without testing it against the clock that will judge it (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:136-137, 438`). No existing agent row records the rotation interval. Not a duplicate.

**At the new seam.** The node drain's tree settles that `kubectl drain` holds no server, CA, user, token, profile or expiry of its own to compare against (`KD: pkg/cmd/drain/drain.go:153-158`, `:225-234`, `:254`), so a `kubectl drain`, `cordon` or `uncordon` in a Run Command document authenticates, if the Kubernetes client hands the script's environment to the exec plugin (seam: client-go), with the principal `SSM-E1`'s substitution selects, inside the windows `SSM-E8`, `SSM-T2` and `SSM-D13` describe, or halts with the CLI's exit 255 on an unparseable prefix (`SSM-T2`). The agent's environment reaches every process the script starts (scope extension (script environment) `SSM: agent/executers/executers.go:468`, `:495`; inheritance by the child's children inferred, seam: Go `os/exec`); the kubeconfig the CLI writes names `command: aws` running `eks get-token` (`CLI: awscli/customizations/eks/update_kubeconfig.py:386-411`), and the token command signs with whatever the chain resolved (`CLI: awscli/customizations/eks/get_token.py:113-117`, `:132`). What the cluster maps that principal to is a seam (the authenticator, RBAC). No row is added: the agent-side check is `SSM-E1`'s.

#### HS3. A step through chronyd's command socket puts every idempotency entry outside its window for the next sweep, so a redelivered command inside its window runs again (deployment assumption: the service's redelivery after the acknowledgement, a seam; no configuration)

**Packages and edge.** chrony's command channel and step path, the kernel clock and the filesystem mtime, the agent's idempotency sweep and receipt check.

**Entry points.**
- Required, `CMDMON`, B2: a `makestep` request with a pending correction of at least 30 minutes that puts the host clock ahead, as HS1, with the same `settime` and start-time branches.
- One cause, `NTP-RESP`, B3: the pending correction (`CH-C1`, `CH-T7`).
- The reader, `AWS-API`: a redelivery of a command already acknowledged. Whether the service redelivers after the MDS acknowledgement is unsettled (Part E, Still unsettled; seam: AWS-API).

**Steps.**
1. As HS1 steps 1 and 2, with a forward step of 30 minutes or more.
2. Each received command creates a directory named by its command id; the filesystem stamps its mtime from the kernel clock at creation (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/idempotency/idempotency.go:84-96`; the stamp inferred, seam: the kernel and the filesystem).
3. The sweep, every ten minutes (`SSM-T6` mechanism, `SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/messagehandler.go:64, 126`), lists entries whose mtime is before the host clock minus 30 minutes (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/idempotency/idempotency.go:60` `time.Now().Add(-30m)`) and deletes them, the pass ending once one document-type directory reaches 200 deletions (`:66` `deletionLimit`, set at `:32`), with Info at the start and end of the pass (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/messagehandler.go:127, 129`) and Debug per deletion (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/idempotency/idempotency.go:59-80`; seam `SSM: agent/fileutil/fileutil.go:316`). After a forward step of 30 minutes or more, every entry qualifies. Source-supported except the mtime comparison, which sits in the seam helper.
4. The receipt check is the directory's existence (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/idempotency/idempotency.go:100-113`, `:107` `stat` + `isNotExist`). A redelivery of the same command id after the sweep is not found, is queued and runs (`SSM-T6`, `SSM-R6`); the second run writes a new entry at Info (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/idempotency/idempotency.go:91`). Source-supported.
5. The service redelivers. Inferred, seam: AWS-API.

**Seam crossed.** chronyd's step path to the kernel clock; the kernel clock to the filesystem mtime and to the sweep's `time.Now()` (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/idempotency/idempotency.go:60`); the sweep to the receipt check.

**Combined impact.** Distance 1: a command runs a second time on the host, with one act outside both trees, the service's redelivery, between the sweep and the run. Halt: none. chronyd's gap alone moves the clock; the agent's gap alone lets a redelivery after 30 real minutes run again; joined, every entry falls outside the window at the moment of the step, and the next sweep deletes them up to its deletion limit. Records: WARN in chronyd (`CH: local.c:707`); Info at the start and end of the sweep (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/messagehandler.go:127, 129`), Debug per deletion (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/idempotency/idempotency.go:74`), and Info "writing command in the idempotency directory" for the second run (`SSM: agent/messageservice/messagehandler/idempotency/idempotency.go:91`). The backward direction is safe (Part E, What the seams close).

**Composition.** `CH-T1`, `CH-S4`, `CH-E1`, `CH-C1`, `CH-T7`, joined to `SSM-T6`, `SSM-R6` and the agent's continue-on-fault path for an idempotency cleanup listing error, carried as new row `SSM-T13`. Chrony-side gap: as HS1. Agent-side gap: the duplicate window is a wall-clock difference against an mtime the same clock set, and on intake the message's own `CreatedDate` is present but unread for age (`SSM: agent/messageservice/utils/messageutil.go:84-86, 100`); row `SSM-T6` records the window. Not a duplicate.

**At the new seam.** The node-lifecycle trees settle that a redelivered drain document after the step does not compound: a second drain of an emptied, cordoned node writes nothing to the cluster, the cordon finding the node already cordoned and printing it (`KD: pkg/cmd/drain/drain.go:423-429`) and the empty pod list returning before any eviction (`KD: pkg/cmd/drain/drain.go:382`; `KD: pkg/drain/drain.go:244-247`). A second reboot request made while one is pending is dropped (extension `SSM: agent/rebooter/rebooter.go:55-61`); those lines do not settle a redelivery that runs after the host has come back up, and on the handler's side such a second reboot has `N-T10`'s effect once, because the first uncordon removes the labels the uptime test needs (`NTH: pkg/node/node.go:625-629`; `NTH: cmd/node-termination-handler.go:313-319`). The same forward step reaching M2 is a parallel effect of one entry, with no artifact flowing between the handler's store or labels and the agent's idempotency entries; M1 needs the clock behind, the opposite direction to this chain's step. M1 records on the handler's side the pattern this chain's composition records on the agent's: a server-issued time present at intake and unread, there the queue's `SentTimestamp` (`NTH: pkg/monitor/sqsevent/sqs-monitor.go:307-309`), here the message's `CreatedDate`.

### Group AS: the chain that crosses between the CLI and the agent

#### AS1. Force-store or purge removes a named profile's keys; the CLI's name-only profile check lets the instance role answer for it (source-supported, EC2 only)

**Preconditions.** EC2 identity. Default host management in use: the agent's credential source is Systems Manager, which with an instance profile attached means the instance-profile path failed at the last retrieve with `AccessDeniedException` or `AssumeRoleUnauthorizedAccess` (the attached role refused by Systems Manager) or with `EC2RoleRequestError` (its credentials not obtained from the metadata service) (`SSM: common/identity/credentialproviders/ec2roleprovider/ec2_role_provider.go:136-148`; `SSM: common/identity/credentialproviders/ec2roleprovider/ec2_role_provider_deps.go:41-45`, confirming line). An instance profile attached (inferred, seam: IMDS and IAM). An operator profile `P` whose keys sit in `/var/lib/amazon/ssm/credentials` (`SSM: agent/appconfig/constants_unix.go:112`) or `%ProgramFiles%\Amazon\SSM\credentials` (`SSM: agent/appconfig/constants_windows.go:212`); the agent writes only `[default]` there (`SSM: agent/managedInstances/sharedCredentials/shared_Credentials.go:72-74`) and creates the file hardened (`:62`; seam `SSM: agent/fileutil/harden.go:18-38`), so `P` was added by a root-level writer, for example a document running the CLI's configure command with the agent's `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` set (inferred, CLI configure path not opened). A `[profile P]` section in the config file the run reads, holding no credential source of its own (the assume-role, web-identity, SSO, login and process providers find nothing in such a profile, `CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:1616-1617, 1908-1909, 2392-2399, 2670-2673, 1140-1142`). A named run: `AWS_PROFILE=P` from the document, or `--profile P`; the agent never sets `AWS_PROFILE` on EC2 (`SSM: common/identity/credentialproviders/ec2roleprovider/ec2_role_provider.go:234-236`). Unnamed runs are not affected. Configuration defaults involved: `ShouldPurgeInstanceProfileRoleCreds` false (`SSM: agent/appconfig/appconfig.go:137`, not needed: purge call 1 has no flag). `ShareCreds` does not gate EC2: the EC2 provider always shares (`SSM: common/identity/credentialproviders/ec2roleprovider/ec2_role_provider.go:239-241`).

**Entry points.**
- Force-store arm: `SHARED-CREDS` (B2, root-level), content in the agent's file that the vendored ini library cannot load (row `SSM-T3`'s trigger).
- Purge arm: `NONE`, the refresher itself after a credential-source flip to the instance profile (seam: IAM), with a script started before the flip or any process that names the fixed path itself.
- The named run: `SCRIPT-ENV` (B2) or an operator shell (B2).

**Steps.**
1. Agent side, force-store arm. On a non-EC2 source the refresher stores with backoff, then once with `force` (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:414-424`; seam `SSM: agent/backoffconfig/backoffconfig.go:30`). With `force`, when `ini.Load` fails, `Store` replaces the config with `ini.Empty()` and writes only `[default]` (`SSM: agent/managedInstances/sharedCredentials/shared_Credentials.go:84-103`, `:88`). Every other section, including `[P]`, is gone. Recorded at Warn (`SSM: agent/managedInstances/sharedCredentials/shared_Credentials.go:87`; `SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:421`). Gap: the writer treats an unloadable file as replaceable and preserves no other section (row `SSM-T3`).
2. Agent side, purge arm. After a retrieve whose source is the instance profile, the refresher unlinks the whole fixed file unless a document or session worker is running and a 3.2-era audit entry is under three days old (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:376-401`, `:390`, `:393`; `SSM: agent/managedInstances/sharedCredentials/shared_Credentials.go:112-114`; seam `SSM: agent/fileutil/fileutil.go:52-54`). Recorded at Info (`SSM: core/app/credentialrefresher/credentialrefresher.go:391, 406`). Gap: the purge removes every section, not only the agent's (row `SSM-T3`).
3. CLI side. The profile map is the union of section names in the config file and the credentials file (`CLI: awscli/botocore/session.py:260-266, 393-417`). `ProfileNotFound` is raised only when the name is in neither (`CLI: awscli/botocore/session.py:375-379`), so a surviving `[profile P]` keeps `P` valid. The shared-file and config providers return None for a profile with no `aws_access_key_id` (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:1379-1385, 1452-1454`). The chain keeps the container and metadata providers after the profile providers for a named run (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:135-149`); an explicit `--profile` removes only the environment provider (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:92, 151-167`), and `AWS_PROFILE` removes nothing. The metadata provider returns the instance role (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:1150-1177`). Gap: the CLI's named-profile check tests that the name exists, not that the named profile supplied the credentials, so a named run that finds no keys is answered by the instance role with no error. Nothing is written below ERROR (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:70, 1166-1168, 2232`; `CLI: awscli/clidriver.py:643-660`).

**Seam crossed.** The agent's writer (`SSM: agent/managedInstances/sharedCredentials/shared_Credentials.go:88`, seam `SSM: vendor/gopkg.in/ini.v1/file.go:511`) or purge (seam `SSM: agent/fileutil/fileutil.go:52-54`) to the CLI session's profile map and resolver, along the rewritten or unlinked file. Then the process to the metadata service and to every service the instance role reaches (inferred, seam: IMDS and AWS-API).

**Combined impact.** Distance 0. A run that names `P` signs as the instance profile role instead of `P`. Before a force-store, `P` resolved to its own keys, or halted with exit 255 when the file was unparseable (scope extension, CLI parse error); after it, the same run resolves to the instance role with no error. The writer's gap alone destroys `P`'s keys, and a run naming `P` would then find nothing and fail. The CLI's name-only check alone, with `P`'s keys intact, changes nothing. Together the guard that makes a named run fail closed is bypassed. The agent records the loss at Warn or Info and never the substitution; the CLI records nothing. Which role carries more permission is set by IAM (seam). Halt: none on either side. On-premises the same steps end in `NoCredentialsError` (inferred, no metadata service, seam: host network), a halt, which is row `SSM-T3` with a CLI halt and not part of this chain.

**Composition.** `SSM-T3` (force-store and purge) joined to the CLI's named-profile rule, which raises `ProfileNotFound` only for a named profile absent from the merged map of both files; agent halt paths: none (continue-on-fault paths: store failure, purge failure). `CLI:` lines: `CLI: awscli/botocore/session.py:260-266, 375-379, 393-417`; `CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:92, 135-149, 151-167, 1150-1177, 1379-1385, 1452-1454`; logging `CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:70, 1166-1168, 2232`, `CLI: awscli/clidriver.py:643-660`.

### Group H: chains inside chrony

#### H1 (`CH-C1`). An unauthenticated response becomes the sole reference (source-supported)

**Entry points.**
- `NTP-RESP`, B3, required: whoever can answer as, or in place of, more than half of the selectable sources and can supply the outstanding request's origin timestamp. With one configured source that is one source. The source count has no tree default: the source list is created empty (`CH: conf.c:389`) and filled only by parsed lines (`CH: conf.c:816`); the count a deployment configures is inferred, seam: the distribution configuration.
- `CONFIG`, B2, one cause: an instance with `nts` 0 and `authkey` 0 (`CH: srcparams.h:85`, extension srcparams.h). That a plain `server` line yields it is inferred, seam `cmdparse.c` (`CH: cmdparse.c:66, 70`).

**Steps.**
1. The instance is NONE (`CH: ntp_core.c:642-646`). Source-supported given the entry precondition.
2. The authentication check passes a response on mode equality alone; a packet with no MAC parses as NONE (`CH: ntp_auth.c:307-312`; `CH: ntp_core.c:1461, 1544-1546`). Source-supported.
3. The only binding to the request is test 2, the echoed origin timestamp; client precision is 32 (`CH: ntp_core.c:1098, 1193-1206, 1811-1815`). Its full randomisation is inferred, seam `util.c` (`CH: util.c:588-603`). Tests 1, 3, 6, 7, A, C and D compare the response with itself, the instance's own history or fixed bounds (`CH: ntp_core.c:1805-1841, 1968-2001`). Test B passes whenever `maxdelayratio` is below 1 (`CH: ntp_core.c:1568-1571`); that the parser default leaves it below 1 is inferred, seam `cmdparse.c`. Source-supported except the randomisation and the parser default.
4. The selection observer cannot fail with one selectable source: 1 against 0 at `CH: sources.c:1079-1080`; `minsources` 1 (`CH: conf.c:159`); after three samples (`CH: regress.h:70`; `CH: regress.c:245-247`) the source is selected and `REF_SetReference` runs (`CH: sources.c:1245-1298`). Source-supported.
5. The reference's `maxchange` and `makestep` checks are off at the tree default (`CH: conf.c:152-153, 163`; `CH: reference.c:544-545, 557-558`), so the offset is slewed (`CH: reference.c:1054-1064`) within only `maxdrift`, the slew clamp, the driver bound and the sanity bound (`CH: local.c:419-441`; `CH: sys_generic.c:219-223, 234`; bound content inferred, seam `util.c`). Source-supported.
6. The kernel frequency and offset are written (`CH: reference.c:1064`; `CH: local.c:594-629`; `CH: sys_linux.c:156-160`). Reader effect inferred, seam: the clock readers.

**Seam crossed.** The authentication check (`CH: ntp_auth.c:303-330`) to the selection observer (`CH: sources.c:787-1299`) along the accumulated sample, the selection observer to the reference's `maxchange` and `makestep` checks (`CH: reference.c:554-576, 541-550`) along `REF_SetReference`, then the kernel seam to every reader.

**Combined impact.** Distance 0. A party reachable from B3, checked only against its own data, its echoed origin timestamp and fixed bounds, sets the clock every process reads. The authentication check's gap alone yields a sample that agreeing sources forming more than half of the selectable set outvote (`CH: sources.c:1079-1094, 1128-1130`); the selection observer's gap alone moves nothing without an accepted sample; the reference's missing bound alone needs a selected input. Halt: none. "Selected source" INFO once (`CH: sources.c:1252`); WARN "System clock wrong by" at the accepting update above `logchange` 1.0 s (`CH: reference.c:498-499, 1067`; `CH: conf.c:172`). Configuration: the source count and the parser default, both inferred, seams: the distribution configuration and `cmdparse.c`.

**Repudiation note.** A response failing test 5 leaves no trace above DEBUG (`CH-R1`; `CH: ntp_core.c:2109-2221, 2279`). That record is the authentication check's reporting channel, not a second observer.

**Composition.** `CH-S1` + `CH-S2` + `CH-T7`, structure `CH-E3`, across the authentication check, the selection observer, and the `maxchange` and `makestep` checks; note `CH-R1`. Preconditions: an instance with `nts` 0 and key 0, which a plain `server` line yields by the parser default (inferred, seam `cmdparse.c`); with one source, every remaining check uses the response itself, its own origin timestamp or fixed bounds (`CH: ntp_core.c:1811-1841, 1968-2001`); at the tree default `makestep` never steps and `maxchange` never checks (`CH: reference.c:541-550, 554-576`; `CH: conf.c:152-153, 163`). Halt: none.

#### A1 (`CLI-C1`). The expiry rewrite defeats the still-expired halt (source-supported)

**Entry points.** IMDS, a credential whose `Expiration` falls inside 1020 to 1500 s of now or has already passed. The service itself needs no actor; a responder on the path is B2 (inferred, seam network; address constant `CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:86` outside the ranges).

1. The fetcher builds the credential dict and calls `_evaluate_expiration` before returning (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:543-552`).

With the window 900 s (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:78, 101, 117`) plus `randint(120, 600)` (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:630-635`), a value at or past `expiration - window` is replaced with now plus the window (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:640-645`). No copy of the service value is kept (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:544-550`). Holds for the format `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` (`CLI: awscli/botocore/utils.py:627-629`).

It fetches again (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:1175, 573-578`) and rewrites again, so remaining falls under 600 s only when no signing call arrives inside the advisory window. Nothing counts the cycles.

**Seam crossed.** The fetcher's expiry rewrite writes the value that the credential object's still-expired check (the CLI's halt path 2) reads. Then the process to STS and the target services, which decide whether keys past the stated expiry are honoured (inferred, seam AWS-API).

Halt: none while the fetcher returns four fields. Remaining halts: a fetcher that raises, once remaining falls under 600 s (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:603-607`); an empty answer (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:612, 640-645`); an `Expiration` in another format (`CLI: awscli/botocore/credentials.py:627` then fires). ### Group KB: keepalived and OpenBao

#### KB-SX1. An OpenBao seal or step-down becomes a keepalived failover with no correlated alert

**Risk and impact.** When OpenBao seals or steps down on the node that holds the VIP, its health endpoint flips to 503 or 429, the keepalived tracker faults after two to four seconds, and the VIP is released and picked up by a peer while OpenBao independently re-elects a new active node. A privileged insider holding a root token can trigger this deliberately, or it happens with no actor at all on a fault-driven seal or leadership loss. No secret is exposed and the write path is not halted: the cluster keeps serving from a new node, but the VIP is left unowned for a computed window of roughly 7.6 to 11.6 seconds plus the delegated Raft election. keepalived logs a script failure and FAULT and OpenBao logs the seal at Info, but neither log names the other system and the joining probe is unaudited, so the two halves are never correlated.

- **Pattern.** A. The weighted-tracker case is row X6, not part of this chain.
- **Entry points.**
  - OB, one cause, B3 with a root token or B1. Source-supported. A seal (halt paths 1, 2, 4,
    6, and the root-token seal) sets `sealed=true`; a step-down or leadership loss (halt path
    7 and the root-token step-down) sets `standby=true`. Required.
  - KA, the reader. Inferred. The Pattern A tracker on every node polls the local health
    endpoint. Required.
- **Step 1, the OpenBao halt reaches health. Source-supported.** `sealInternalWithOptions`
  sets the flag with a compare-and-swap at `OB: internal/vault/core.go:2074`, the first
  statement of the function (`2072-2076`) and ahead of every teardown step; `Sealed()` reads it
  at `OB: core.go:1455-1457`. A step-down or leadership loss stores `standby=true` at
  `OB: internal/vault/ha.go:985`. `/sys/health` reads both atomics at
  `OB: internal/http/sys_health.go:118-119` and selects 503 when sealed (`138-139`) and 429
  when standby without `standbyok` (`140-143`). Seam: the OpenBao process to its own HTTP
  listener.
- **Step 2, the tracker fails. Inferred probe, source-supported gating.** The tracker script
  `curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/health` exits non-zero on 429, 501 and 503 (inferred;
  curl is in neither tree). `vrrp_script_thread` re-arms itself with
  `thread_add_timer(..., vscript->interval)` before each run
  (`KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:1254-1255`), so runs are strictly `interval`-periodic and a run
  is skipped only while the previous one is not idle (`1257-1262`).
  `vrrp_script_child_thread` reads a non-zero exit as failure (`1369-1379`) and the counter at
  `1424-1438` requires `fall` consecutive failures before
  `update_script_priorities(vscript, false)` at `1435`. Seam crossed: the OpenBao health answer
  to the keepalived tracker.
- **Step 3, FAULT releases the VIP. Source-supported.** A weight-0 track script that fails
  reaches `down_instance` (`KA: vrrp/vrrp_track.c:664`, function at `567-587`), which in MASTER
  runs `vrrp_state_leave_master(vrrp, true)` at `580`. That logs FAULT and sends a priority-0
  advert at `KA: vrrp/vrrp.c:2057-2063`, then calls `vrrp_restore_interface` at `2069`, which
  sends priority 0 again with `advF` true at `1993-1998` and deletes the VIPs and eVIPs at
  `2023-2035`.
- **Step 4, a peer takes the VIP while OpenBao re-elects independently. Source-supported on
  both sides, with the election delegated.** Every non-active node's tracker is already failing
  on 429, so every peer is in FAULT, and a FAULT instance processes no advert:
  `KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:1199-1206` dispatches to `vrrp_state_backup` only in BACKUP and to
  `vrrp_state_master_rx` only in MASTER. The priority-0 advert of step 3 therefore reaches no
  listener that can act on it, and the skew shortcut at `KA: vrrp/vrrp.c:2221-2224` is not
  taken. A node leaves FAULT only through `try_up_instance` (`KA: vrrp/vrrp_track.c:671`;
  `KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:695-758`), which sets BACKUP at `748` and the full
  `VRRP_MS_DOWN_TIMER` at `758`. On expiry `vrrp_dispatcher_read_timeout` calls
  `vrrp_goto_master` (`KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:914-918`), which adds the VIPs
  (`KA: vrrp/vrrp.c:1913-1917`) and sends GARP (`1929`). OpenBao's new active node stores
  `standby=false` at `OB: ha.go:932` after `postUnseal` at `930`.
- **The combined window, recomputed.** Terms, in order, for the Pattern A numbers
  (`interval 2`, `fall 2`, `rise 2`, `priority 100`, `advert_int 1`, VRRPv2):
  1. OpenBao flips the health answer. For a seal, zero: the compare-and-swap at
     `OB: core.go:2074` precedes the teardown, so 503 is answered from the first instant. For a
     step-down or leadership loss, the flip at `OB: ha.go:985` follows the select at `950-957`
     and the state-lock grab at `975-977`; the in-flight drain at `964-972` bounds only the
     context cancel, not the store, so this term is bounded by lock contention and is not a
     fixed number in the code.
  2. Detection. Between `(fall - 1) x interval` and `fall x interval`, that is **2 s to 4 s**,
     plus one script round trip, because the first failing probe lands anywhere inside the
     interval and `fall` consecutive failures are needed
     (`KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:1254-1255`, `1424-1438`).
  3. FAULT and VIP removal. One synchronous call chain, `1435` to
     `KA: vrrp/vrrp_track.c:664` to `KA: vrrp/vrrp.c:2023-2035`, plus the netlink round trip.
     Not a scheduled delay.
    4. The new active node. **Storage-dependent.** Under the reference joint deployment the storage
     is PostgreSQL, so the leader-loss channel consumed at `OB: ha.go:951` is closed by
     `periodicallyRenewLock` (`OB: internal/physical/postgresql/postgresql.go:703-719`,
     `close(done)` at `707`), and a peer becomes active by taking the lock row
     (`OB: internal/physical/postgresql/postgresql.go:233-239`), bounded above by the 15 s lock
     TTL (`33`), the 5 s renew interval (`36`) and the 1 s acquire retry (`40`). Under Raft
     integrated storage the same channel is closed from
     `OB: internal/physical/raft/raft.go:2007-2010` and the term is the Raft election
     (`OB: go.mod:75`), delegated and not computed here.
  5. The new active node's tracker rises. Between `(rise - 1) x interval` and
     `rise x interval`, that is **2 s to 4 s**, plus one round trip: the failing tracker sits at
     `result = 0` and the counter at `KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:1415-1423` needs `rise`
     consecutive successes before `update_script_priorities(vscript, true)` at `1420`.
  6. That node becomes MASTER. `try_up_instance` sets the full master-down timer
     (`KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:758`), which is `down_timer_adverts x master_adver_int + skew`
     (`KA: include/vrrp.h:511`), with `down_timer_adverts` 3 (`KA: include/vrrp.h:166`;
     `KA: core/global_data.c:115`) and `skew = (256 - effective_priority) x TIMER_HZ / 256`
     (`KA: include/vrrp.h:508-509`), giving 3 + 0.609 = **3.609 s** at priority 100.

    Sum of the computed terms, from the health flip to a peer holding the VIP:
  **2 s to 4 s (detection) + the re-election term of term 4 + 2 s to 4 s (rise) + 3.609 s
  (master-down timer)**, plus two script round trips and the netlink and packet latencies. With
  the election term set aside, the computed floor is 7.6 s and the computed ceiling is 11.6 s.
  Assumptions the number rests on, each a deployment choice or a term outside both trees: the
  Pattern A values `interval 2`, `fall 2`, `rise 2` and no `weight`; VRRPv2 with
  `advert_int 1` and `priority 100` on every instance and no `nopreempt` or `preempt_delay`;
  the default `down_timer_adverts` of 3; the curl completing inside one interval, so no run is
  skipped at `KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:1257-1262`; the tracker script exec-ing successfully,
  which SX7 shows is not guaranteed; a single VRRP instance with no sync group; and the health
  flip being observed by the very next probe rather than one later.
- **Seam.** OpenBao's seal and standby atomics to the keepalived tracker, and from there to the
  kernel's address table and to the VRRP segment.
- **Combined impact.** Distance 0. The halt does not reach customer data; it moves the VIP.
  Under the default weight-0 tracker the cluster keeps serving from a new node, with the VIP
  unowned for the computed window above, and no alert correlates the two halves. keepalived
  logs `VRRP_Script(...) failed` and `Entering FAULT STATE`
  (`KA: vrrp/vrrp_scheduler.c:1432-1434`; `KA: vrrp/vrrp.c:2058`); OpenBao logs
  `marked as sealed` and `vault is sealed` at Info (`OB: core.go:2079`, `2178`). Neither line
  names the other system, and the probe that joined them is unaudited (SX10). Actor B3 with a
  root token, or B1.
- **Composition.** keepalived halt path 14 (Instance FAULT), KA gap 6 Death Signaling, KA gap 1
  Heartbeat; OB halt paths 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, `OB D "Seal and step-down"`,
  `OB D "Leadership loss"`, `OB T "sys/health meaning"`, OB availability claim 17, left
  unevaluated.

**Under Vault (holds with changed citations).** The chain runs as written with re-cited lines. `sealInternalWithOptions` sets `c.sealed` with a compare-and-swap at `VA: vault/core.go:2543`, ahead of teardown, and `Sealed()` reads it at `VA: vault/core.go:1778-1779`; a leadership loss or manual step-down stores `c.standby = true` at `VA: vault/ha.go:756`. `sys/health` answers 503 when sealed (`VA: http/sys_health.go:206-207`) and 429 when standby without `standbyok` (`:216-219`).
